⚙️ Трезвый взгляд на ABI после 2000 часов в Таркове. Стоит ли играть? Cмог ли китайский гигант Tencent сделать убийцу главного экстракшен-шутера?

Если коротко: Нет, не убил. Но заставил Буянова попотеть.
Ниже разложу по полочкам, почему ABI - это одновременно глоток свежего воздуха и спорный продукт.

🟢 Что реально порадовало
+ Запуск за секунды. Загрузка в рейд идет секунд 30. Умер? Через минуту ты уже снова на карте в полной экипировке. Никаких «Ожиданий игроков» по 10 минут.
+ Игра не превращается в работу. Сюда не нужно заходить как на вторую смену. Захотел пострелять - зашел, кайфанул часик и спокойно вышел. Никакой обязаловки.
+ Нет тупых квестов. Нас избавили от маразма в духе «убей 15 ЧВК в прыжке с завязанными глазами». И главное - никаких квестов, которые тебя заставляют уныло перепроходить после каждого вайпа.
+ Читеров намного меньше. По моим ощущениям, в разы. Да, софтеры бывают везде, но тут они не встречаются в каждом втором рейде.
+ Античит работает на вас. Если вас всё-таки убил читер и его потом забанили - игра возвращает вам весь потерянный лут. Вот за это прям огромный респект разработчикам.
+ Игра не тормозит. Оптимизация на удивление отличная. FPS стабильный, картинка сочная, фризов в перестрелках нет.
+ Удобно играть. Человеческий интерфейс, понятная карта прямо в игре, нормальные маркеры. Не нужно держать открытой Википедию на втором мониторе, чтобы понять, куда идти.

🔴 Что напрягает
- Донат. Да, игра бесплатная, но Tencent хочет денег. Валюту можно купить за реал, а безопасный контейнер дают только по платной подписке. Без доната на высоких уровнях копить деньги на топовый шмот будет тяжело.
- Тесные карты. Локации довольно зажатые, из-за чего ПвП часто начинается в первые 20 секунд после спавна. Вас просто зажимают с двух сторон.
- Меньше атмосферы. Игра ощущается как стерильный хардкорный шутер в стиле Call of Duty. Тут нет того подкожного страха и безысходности, как в Таркове.

⚖️ Прямое сравнение: ABI vs EFT

* Порог входа: В ABI всё понятно сразу, обучение дружелюбное. В Таркове нужно страдать первые сотни часов, заучивая выходы по сторонним картам.
* Работа игры: ABI летает даже на средних ПК и быстро загружается. Таркову нужно топовое железо, ССД и куча терпения.
* Суть лута: В ABI всё упрощено - важна только цена предмета на рынке. В Таркове каждый болт, провод и туалетная бумага нужны для Убежища и квестов.
* Боёвка: В ABI она более быстрая, динамичная и аркадная. В Таркове - медленная, позиционная, с тяжелой инерцией движений.
* Прогрессия: В ABI ты просто играешь в свое удовольствие. В Таркове игра заставляет тебя упарываться в гринд квестов ради торговцев.

📣 Итог
Arena Breakout: Infinite - это качественный, быстрый фастфуд. Если у вас мало времени после работы, вы устали от багов и хотите просто зайти и пострелять - игра идеальна. Она бесплатная, так что попробовать точно стоит. Но если вам нужна глубокая атмосфера выживания и вы готовы ради этого терпеть боль - Тарков остаётся на своём месте. Для бесплатного проекта — крепкие 7.5 из 10.

Если обзор помог определиться - закиньте лайк или награду, буду благодарен!


⚙️ A sober look at the ABI after 2000 hours in Tarkov. Is it worth playing? Could the Chinese giant Tencent make the killer of the main extraction shooter?

In short: No, he did not. But he made Buyanov sweat.
Below I will break down why ABI is both a breath of fresh air and a controversial product.

🟢 What really pleased me
+ Start in seconds. Loading into the raid takes about 30 seconds. Died? In a minute, you are back on the map in full gear. No "Player Expectations" for 10 minutes.
+ Play does not turn into work. You don't need to come here as a second shift. If you want to shoot, you go in, enjoy an hour and calmly go out. No obligation.
+ No dumb quests. We were saved from insanity in the spirit of "kill 15 PMCs in a jump blindfolded." And most importantly - no quests that make you sadly replay after each wipe.
+ There are much fewer cheaters. According to my feelings, at times. Yes, there are softers everywhere, but here they are not found in every second raid.
+ Anti-cheat works for you. If you are killed by a cheater and then banned, the game returns you all the lost loot. For this, a huge respect to the developers.
+ The game does not slow down. The optimisation is surprisingly excellent. The FPS is stable, the picture is juicy, there are no freezes in the shootouts.
+ Easy to play. Human interface, a clear map right in the game, normal markers. You don't need to keep Wikipedia open on a second monitor to figure out where to go.

🔴 What is stressful
- Donation. Yes, the game is free, but Tencent wants money. Currency can be bought for real, and a secure container is given only with a paid subscription. Without donations at high levels, it will be difficult to save money for top clothes.
- Cramped maps. The locations are quite tight, which is why PvP often starts in the first 20 seconds after spawning. You are simply clamped on both sides.
- Less atmosphere. The game feels like a sterile hardcore shooter in the style of Call of Duty. There is no subcutaneous fear and hopelessness as in Tarkov.

⚖️ Direct comparison: ABI vs EFT

* Entry threshold: In ABI, everything is clear at once, the training is friendly. In Tarkov, you have to suffer for the first hundreds of hours, memorising exits on third-party maps.
* Game Operation: ABI flies even on average PCs and loads quickly. Tarkov needs top hardware, SJS and a lot of patience.
* Loot essence: In ABI, everything is simplified - only the price of the item on the market is important. In Tarkov, every bolt, wire, and toilet paper is needed for the Vault and quests.
* Combat: In ABI, it is faster, more dynamic, and more arcade-like. In Tarkov - slow, positional, with heavy inertia of movements.
* Progression: In ABI, you just play for fun. In Tarkov, the game forces you to grind quests for merchants.

📣 Conclusion
Arena Breakout: Infinite is a high-quality, fast-paced fast food experience. If you don't have much time after work, you're tired of bugs, and you just want to go in and shoot, the game is perfect. It's free, so it's definitely worth a try. But if you need a deep atmosphere of survival and you are ready to endure pain for this, Tarkov remains in his place. For a free project, it's a solid 7.5 out of 10.

If the review helped you decide - throw a like or an award, I will be grateful!

This game had every ingredient to be the extraction shooter that honest players could actually call home — and the devs wasted it.

Let's start with the most obvious rot: cheating. Not casual cheating. Organized, commercial cheating. There are entire supply networks — storefronts, Discord servers, subscription services — openly selling hacks for this game. Speed hacks, ESP, aimbot, full suites. The cheating infrastructure is so mature it has customer support. I've spent time identifying these accounts, studying their behavioral patterns, even tracing the supply chains back to the sellers. You know what the devs have done with that information? Nothing that matters.

The anti-cheat is cosmetic. A system that can be bypassed by suppliers who've clearly had months — if not longer — to reverse-engineer it. Bans happen slowly if at all, and the accounts come right back. The developers know this ecosystem exists. They benefit from it passively because cheaters keep buying the game, keep buying Bonds, keep fueling the economy. Banning them aggressively would hurt the bottom line, and that tells you everything you need to know about where the priorities are.

Then there's the economy. The vault storage system is designed to squeeze you — permanent upgrades tied behind grind or cash, with E-Box "rentals" that disappear at season's end. The game is structured to make you feel like you're progressing while actually running in place, and the Koen economy is balanced around the assumption that a percentage of your lobby is cheating and extracting more than should be physically possible.

This could have been something real. The extraction shooter genre is starving for a game that takes its player base seriously. ABI has the map design, the tension, the moment-to-moment feel of something that works — and then you run into your third rage-cheater of the session and remember what you're actually dealing with.

The devs aren't struggling to fix this. They're choosing not to. There's a difference.

Don't waste your time or your money here. The house always wins, and in this case, the house is also selling aimbots. 

To the Devs: Apologizing while not addressing infrastructure is not zero-tolerance. Zero tolerance means storefronts with 50k+ sales and 24/7 support don't exist openly. They do. That's not an "ongoing battle" - that's an unaddressed market you pretend not to see.

Funny: my emails got zero response, but a review turning buyers away gets a PR reply in a month. You didn't find conscience - you found a revenue threat. Save the performance for someone who hasn't watched you ignore documented cheating operations.

Since your "commitment to improvement" - I came back. Took your survey. First game? Empty map, just AI. Second and third? Died to aimbot/walls. Two of three. Nothing's fixed. You're not "limiting cheat effectiveness" - you limit email replies to what hurts your wallet.

The house still wins. You just don't like players counting cards (they have now hidden this review.)

I really enjoyed ABI during my first 50 hours. It was the best extraction shooter I've played. Unfortunately, the more I played, the more the game started to disappoint me.

What I Like

1. The Loot System
The loot system is excellent. You always know exactly what you've picked up and how much it's worth, thanks to the clear value and color . It makes looting quite satisfying.

2. Gunplay and Weapon Selection
The gunplay feels great, and there's a wide selection of weapons and attachments to play with. That said, the current so called meta means most players use the same 5 guns.

3. The Feeling of Security
If you die with a 1 mil kit at the start of a raid, i would be fuming. However, unlike many other extraction games it's relatively easy to get Koen again. Between the different free Gear/Money rewards, you're rarely left completely broke.

4. No Pay-to-Win
While I think the skin prices are absurd with a dumb gacha system, the game itself isn't pay-to-win, which deserves credit. That's becoming increasingly rare in free-to-play games.

What I Dislike

1. Solo Nightmare
The game constantly caters to four-man squads. The solo mode is a complete joke since you can only play two maps, and there are no Normal or Lockdown modes. Auto Match? Nope. It doesn't work. I've tried countless times to queue with Auto Match enabled, but it rarely happens. The game desperately needs a proper solo mode.

2. Arcade Direction
Lately, it feels like it's moving toward a more arcade style direction with increasingly over the top skins that don't fit the game 

3. Events
ABI has an ungodly amount of ongoing events at all times, to the point where I don't even know if I'm playing the same game anymore.

4. Gear Balance
Armor feels useless at close range, but as soon as you get 1 meter out of effective range, your bullets feel like they do nothing. There are only about five guns worth using. You can also bring high-tier ammunition into lower-level lobbies, which is an unfair advantage in my opinion.

5. Cheaters
The cheating problem has gotten really bad. I constantly get instantly one-tapped in the head, and then I watch the kill cam only to see someone tracking me through walls. And reporting feels useless

Conclusion

I genuinely enjoy ABI when I'm playing with friends. The core gameplay is fun, the extraction mechanics are solid, and the loot system is the best in any extactin shooter so far i played.

However, when I play solo, the game becomes incredibly frustrating. Between the lack of solo options, awful balancing, and the increasing number of cheaters, the experience quickly becomes negetiv.

The game has so much potential. And it's great in many ways but I think it's heading in the wrong direction.

I started playing ABI in the middle of S1, and it felt like a realistic extraction shooter.  Unfortunately, every new season pushes it further away from that identity.

The matchmaking is terrible: T6 players with thermals are regularly paired against players running budget kits.  Gun balance has also become a mess!  Fights no longer feel realistic; it often takes entire magazines to down someone, while weapons that should be devastating (like the Mosin) can require multiple headshots just to do meaningful damage.  The game increasingly feels like an arcade shooter rather than a tactical extraction game.

Cheating is another huge problem.  Most cheaters receive only temporary bans, return quickly, and players who lose expensive gear get no compensation or rollback.

The monetization is also hard to justify.  The game is free, but many cosmetic bundles are around $100+, and instead of military-themed gear, the game is filled with anime, cyberpunk, fantasy armor, swords and other unrealistic cosmetics.

Honestly, the only consistently impressive part of ABI is the graphics, if you have a powerful enough PC to run it.  Every update makes the game heavier and more demanding while the gameplay quality keeps declining.


Rating: 2/10 - great graphics, but poor matchmaking, bad weapon balance, rampant cheating, and a complete loss of the realistic atmosphere that made the game popular in the first place.

At the time of writing this review, I have logged nearly 900 hours, constantly running red raids, actively moving around the maps, and mostly playing in duos or full squads, Throughout my time in the game, I have successfully extracted with over 1 billion worth of loot, killed nearly 2,000 players, and dealt over 1 million in total damage. I know almost every single spawn point on every map, and I am fully familiar with various tactics for close-quarters combat or pushing any point of interest. Here are my conclusions for anyone thinking about starting this game or considering a return:

ABI is an utterly unrewarding, toxic, suffocating, and tedious game that will repeatedly mock you until you completely lose all hope. Why? Let's break it down:

1. TTK (Time to Kill)
It is abysmally fast. It doesn't matter if you are wearing a 3+ million kit (including top-tier ammo, grenades, and consumables) with a fully modded meta weapon, or if you are running naked with a literal pipe instead of a pistol — the outcome is the same: you will die in a split second. 

Addition to this point for clarification: TTK shouldn't require you to dump multiple mags into someone, but it should be high enough for your armor to actually do its job — surviving maybe 15, 20, or 25 bullets (as a rough estimate). To be clear, I am talking about T6 armor specifically, the absolute best gear in the game. When T5 ammo shreds a T6 plate in a split second, it is completely absurd, considering the ammo is a whole tier lower than the armor.

I could understand dying that fast if the enemy was using a hard-hitting rifle like the FAL or MK14 loaded with T6 ammo, but that's not the case. Barely anyone even runs those rifles anyway because of their insane recoil, and despite the guns being cheap, T6 ammo is just ridiculously overpriced.

2. Armor
The most useless and overpriced thing in the game. No body armor or helmet will ever give you enough time to react, turn around, and return fire if you get caught off guard. Even if you somehow survive the initial burst, your armor durability shreds instantly. This leaves you with zero competitive edge, forcing you to either rush to exfil immediately or sit in a bush waiting out the entire raid just to survive. Even T4 ammo from an H416 can melt you in seconds.

3. Playing Solo? Forget it.
If you don't have friends or prefer solo raids — don't even bother. This game hates solo players; it doesn't recognize or reward them in any way. In squad matches, you will constantly face the knockdown mechanic (if you don't instantly finish an enemy, their teammates will just revive them) or squads with perfect info on your location thanks to teammate markers. As for the dedicated solo modes, you get a rotation of just two maps a week. The first is massive and wide open with forests and hills, where you can randomly catch a single red bullet from a bush. The second forces you to check absolutely every corner, otherwise, you'll die to some rat who has been sitting in one spot for 20 minutes just waiting for you.

4. Broken Economy
High-end gear is unjustifiably expensive. Finding the rarest "red" items in a raid will barely cover half the cost of your top-tier kit (or just your T5 ammo supply). Meanwhile, purple and gold items are worth pennies. The loot drop rates in Lockdown raids are terrible. Unless you kill other players (and pray that their gear is worth at least half of what you brought in), the game turns into a tedious looting simulator just to break even on your ammo costs.

5. Loot & Playstyle
Want to know the most consistent way to make money I've found? Playing like an absolute rat. You sit quietly, listen, sniff out all nearby points of interest while everyone else is fighting, and then swoop in to clean up the leftovers and grab some free T5 armor or guns. And even if I die, the most I lose is around 450k... Reminder: I am writing a review for an extraction shooter, not a scavenging simulator.

6. Cheaters
Cheating is a disease in many online games, but in ABI, it’s an incurable cancer. The developers completely ignore it and seem incapable of doing anything. Don't believe me? Just look it up on YouTube or TikTok. There is a massive amount of cheaters literally making content out of this. One streams it live, another shares how they see a cheater with ESP or aimbot in almost every single raid. They don't get banned for weeks — sometimes months.
Because of this, you will constantly run into: Players who always know exactly where you are. Players who land perfect, flawless headshots. Players who will laser-spray you right in the neck (the most vulnerable spot) using T3 ammo on a trash weapon while you are wearing top-tier gear. The game's website has an "Inspector" role for players to review reported gameplay demos, but even that helps absolutely nothing.

Recent Updates
Want to know what they added recently? A new mode with literal superpowers/abilities, and a couple of new guns just to simulate variety among top-tier weapons, while half of the rifles and SMGs in the game remain completely unviable. Not to mention that weapon modding has become completely standardized into a single meta template, killing any real variety or experimentation with different attachments.

Every project has its pros and cons, but this game's pros are so minor that they simply cannot compete with the cons. Essentially, once you hit level 30, you've already seen all the content. You won't find anything new after that, except for various glitches or ways to climb into unintended, out-of-bounds spots to get an unfair advantage.

Summary
What is the final verdict? It's a looting simulator with elements of surviving against cheaters. The weapons are only there to give you the illusion that you actually have a chance to kill someone.

Here is a brief assessment of my take on Abi.
First, let's cover the basics needed to actually enjoy the game.
Do you speak Russian? Do you have enough real money to spend? Are you willing to use hacks?
Do they have no conscience when it comes to the spoils?I’ve been playing ABI since the beginning of Season 3, and I’ve experienced quite a few fun days along the way. Anyone who plays the game—or even just watches a little YouTube—knows the BDC (Inspectors).
The current season is defined by the fact that, out of roughly 30,000 active players, about 20,000 are cheaters who aren't playing legitimately. The remainder consists of players with over 500 million in their stash who are more interested in stealing others' loot—or complaining when it happens to them.Since I mentioned the Inspector program: I’ve been at the highest rank since Season 4, and I have an 89.87% accuracy rate when it comes to spotting cheaters. The result this season is that—unless you happen to be an elite shooter player—you’ll frequently run into a cheater who quickly takes you out and teabags you.
Experienced players generally show little interest in taking new players under their wing—except perhaps to treat them as a source of loot or as bait. Even when you do find someone to play with, it rarely lasts, because the game tempts you to relive the good old days of CS.Insults are the order of the day; putting someone down is a form of affection; and flaming—when you die yourself—is the way of saying "you suck."It feels like this game is populated almost exclusively by English speakers or Russians. Which brings us back to the topic of the good old CS days: insults no one understands and, far too often, all-out hostility.


The support is a marvel in itself; a few tests suggest that if you’ve spent money on these games—and I mean over 100 bucks—you’ll actually get support. That applies if a cheater kills you, or if your teammates kill you just to take your loot.
You do get back the money you spent on gear or loot, but if you think you can play the game without actually spending money, you’re in the wrong place. Besides, there isn't really a good reason to spend money—unless you want to die while wearing a "good-looking" skin.Basically, it’s always the same story: unless you get lucky or are willing to spend a long time figuring out the system, you’ll struggle to make any progress—or won't get anywhere at all. The community is worse than in CS, because we’re playing a loot-extraction shooter here where money is the ultimate measure of everything.And when it comes to loot, many people know no bounds.

The Maps
Some maps can only be played in specific ways; for instance, if you pick the "Armory" map, you pretty much have to be a "rat" who can or wants to snipe—which is considered the worst way to play the game, since everyone whines if you actually play like a real sniper.Or they have plenty of grenades with them, or they’re using a good wallhack and aimbot. Far too often, the match turns into a pure grenade war decided simply by how many grenades each side is carrying.

Valley is a map that anyone can play right from the start; the problem with it, however, is that long-time players know tricks to bypass the maximum gear score limit, allowing them to bring in superior gear or ammunition.When you play this map, you quickly get the feeling that it’s just a hunt for newbies. You do manage to get some good loot now and then, but you have to realize that you can lose it all just as fast because experienced players camp the exits.

TV Station
TV Station is a map designed purely for PvP if you want to make money fast—or risk losing everything—this is the map for you. It is small, fast, and brutal.

People always say it plays really well, but a major problem—especially in the current Season 6—remains the presence of cheaters and YouTube sites advertising undetectable cheats for sale. Most long-time players have a very high stash value and, consequently, a lot to lose.
And the worst part is simply that many people have now adopted the mindset that hate, insults, and flaming are the way the game is supposed to be played.

Pros: The Best Way to Lose Friends
This game says it’s Free to Play… they lied. It costs friendships. You think you’re just dropping in with the boys? Nah. You’re dropping into emotional bankruptcy. One second you’re all laughing; the next, Chad "accidentally" forgets to cover your flank and your million-dollar kit is gone. Now you’re broke AND you hate Chad.

This isn’t just a shooter; it’s a social experiment. Arena Breakout Infinite doesn’t just test your aim—it tests your ability to forgive betrayal, cope with digital poverty, and resist the urge to uninstall Discord. GG devs, you’ve created the first truly "Pay-to-Lose-Friendship" game. 10/10, would get betrayed again.

Cons: A Identity Crisis in Progress
I’m writing this as an extraction veteran and a "Tarkov refugee" who genuinely loves this game. Initially, ABI was everything I wanted: stable servers, great QoL, and a fair chance for average players to take down "sweats" with a well-placed shot. Unfortunately, recent updates are stripping that identity away.

The "Effective Range" Problem: The balance has shifted from skill-based to stat-based. I recently headshot an unhelmeted player with an FAL (T4 ammo), and they survived because of the "Effective Range" mechanic. A flat -30% damage penalty just because a player is 1 meter outside an arbitrary range feels arcadey and punishing. It makes it nearly impossible for a budget player to win via skill.

The "Sweat" Shield: The introduction of craftable self-revives and injectors that reduce limb damage spread has removed the only weakness of T6 "juggernauts." TL;DR: A streamlined version of Escape from Tarkov with close to none technical issues, faster progression, and a much smoother onboarding experience. The game heavily rewards coordinated squad play, making solo play significantly more challenging at higher levels. While I don't personally like the more arcade-like direction the developers have taken recently, it's ultimately a matter of taste.

Tarkov vs. Arena

👍 Where it shines;
- It's free. Unlike Tarkov, you don't have to pay to find out whether you'll like it or is it gonna run on your pc with 256 Gigs of ram and 6G connection.
- Much easier to learn than Tarkov thanks to features like an in-game map, simplified healing, and a more accessible UI.
- Weapon and gear customization is available after roughly 10–20 hours instead of being locked behind hundreds of hours of progression.
- Gearing up for raids doesn't take longer than the raid itself, everything is at reach and user-friendly.
- No friendly fire, making it much easier to team up with random players.
- 800 hours played with zero crashes or major bugs, which is genuinely impressive.
- Stable servers and a much smoother online experience compared to Tarkov.
- Faster-paced PvP with greater freedom to rotate, reposition, disengage, and coordinate thanks to visible teammates and cleverly designed maps and areas.
- The new PvE mode is an excellent addition. You can play solo, with friends, or through matchmaking, and the AI feels challenging without being unfairly aimbot-like.

👎 Where it falls short;
- Solo play becomes extremely difficult at higher-level hence not enjoyable, Expect to face coordinated premade squads. flanking and outplaying multiple opponents is much harder than in Tarkov.
- Recent updates have pushed the game toward a more Call of Duty-style experience, and the general direction of dev is CoD like extraction shooter experience, this will not satisfy those who value realism.
- Colorful cosmetic skins undermine the gritty extraction shooter atmosphere, talking about which, you don't really feel an atmosphere of hardcore harsh environment in-game.
- Severe damage drop-off at range and heavily reduced one-shot potential encourage close-quarters squad fights over long-range engagements. Some players will enjoy this faster-paced style, while others may find it disappointing and arcady.
- Character and weapon animations are noticeably worse than Tarkov's or many other decent shooter games, and can feel like mobile game. This is one area where the developers should invest much more.
- The meta is much more restrictive than in Tarkov. High-level gameplay tends to revolve around the same few weapons and gear loadouts, making matches feel repetitive, whereas Tarkov offers a much wider variety of viable guns, ammunition, and attachments.

Verdict

Arena Breakout is one of the most polished extraction shooters available. It removes much of the frustration associated with Tarkov—technical issues, excessive grinding, and poor accessibility—while keeping the core tactical extraction gameplay intact.

That said, the game has gradually shifted toward a more arcade-focused experience. If you enjoy fast-paced, squad-oriented action, but don't mind it being arcady, you'll probably love the current direction. If you prefer slower, more realistic gunfights with stronger emphasis on long-range engagements and hardcore atmosphere, you may be less enthusiastic.

I would easily recommend this game to anyone interested in extraction shooters who doesn't mind it being a bit arcady, whereas I would seldom recommend Tarkov to someone new—not only because of the initial grind, but also because of its seemingly endless and random technical issues which hardly ever gets fixed.

Rating: 7.5/10
